paragraphs.source_en: Ishikawa Hōki-no-kami Kazumasa left Okazaki and fled to Osaka. To Hideyoshi, who had already moved his great army to the port of Sakai in preparation for an attack on Shikoku, it was no great matter; to the Tokugawa clan, however, it came like a thunderbolt from a clear sky.

paragraphs.source_en: The news was sent to Tokugawa Ieyasu at Hamamatsu by Sakai Saemon-no-jō Tadatsugu of Yoshida Castle before dawn on the fourteenth. While dispatching a messenger to report the matter to his lord, Tadatsugu himself spurred his horse toward Okazaki. Together with Matsudaira Ietada, he reached the castle town at the hour of the Dragon and calmed the agitated townspeople. At that time, of course, neither Tadatsugu nor Ietada knew whether Kazumasa truly meant to flee or was attempting to deceive the enemy.
